quotes.text: [Checkout](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout.md) and [Elements](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/elements.md) automatically apply the best practices recommended in this guide.
DPANs are tied to the specific Apple device, and can be unintentionally deactivated if a user switches to a new device
When the first CIT using the cryptogram fails, subsequent MITs using the same [Card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/cards/object.md) will likely also fail because they’re internally linked to the CIT.
We discourage using the legacy Tokens and Charges APIs for recurring Apple Pay payments.

Apple Pay terms forbid using a saved payment method for [usage=on_session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object.md#setup_intent_object-usage) payments. If the customer is in the flow, you’re required to have them authorize and generate a new cryptogram for that transaction.

findings: The November same-URL page adds no substantive Apple Pay recurring contract: the collection diff changes list numbering, whitespace and blank lines only (diff lines 3-49). Both raw captures retain the CIT/cryptogram timing, DPAN/MPAN, free-trial SetupIntent, legacy Tokens/Charges migration advice, and saved on-session restriction. This is a corrective source disposition, not a newly announced capability.

The current source materially overstates three pre-existing claims: DPAN 'deactivates' on device change rather than 'can be unintentionally deactivated' (source line 20; new line 20); failed CIT makes 'all subsequent MITs' fail rather than 'will likely also fail' (source line 23; new line 28); and Tokens API is called 'strongly deprecated' rather than discouraged for recurring Apple Pay with migration recommended (source line 29; new lines 48-54). The linked stripe-wallets concept repeats the latter two absolutes at line 125.

The source's 'Checkout/Elements handle this automatically' point is retained by the new capture (new line 11). The free-trial Subscription-created SetupIntent and direct SetupIntent alternatives remain at new lines 40-44; saved off-session payments still lack network liability shift and may have lower authorization rates at new line 77.

The saved-payment usage=on_session ban remains an explicit Apple Pay terms restriction at new lines 79-81. It should be scoped to using a saved payment method while the customer is in the flow; the user must authorize and generate a fresh cryptogram for that transaction.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Checkout and Elements automatically apply the guide's best practices (old line 10; new line 11).

CIT must consume the expiring cryptogram promptly; a Subscription trial SetupIntent or directly confirmed SetupIntent can perform a 0 USD validation before later off-session MIT use (old lines 23-43; new lines 24-44).

Stripe discourages legacy Tokens and Charges for recurring Apple Pay, recommends PaymentIntents and SetupIntents, and documents a Tokens-to-PaymentMethod-to-SetupIntent bridge (old lines 45-72; new lines 46-71).

Saved off-session use is supported with liability-shift/authorization-risk caveats, while saved on-session use requires fresh customer authorization and a cryptogram (old lines 74-91; new lines 73-90).
conflicts: Existing source lines 20, 23 and 29 and stripe-wallets concept line 125 use absolute failure/deactivation or formal-deprecation wording that neither the old nor new raw supports. Correct those retained claims without implying a November policy change.

The source line 17 says the guide applies to direct API integrations only, but the page includes general recurring Apple Pay behavior and states Checkout/Elements automatically apply its practices (new lines 9-28); scope the manual implementation steps to API integrations.
unresolved_questions: Neither capture supplies a fixed cryptogram lifetime, a measured authorization improvement, or a guarantee that every MPAN survives all card/device lifecycle changes.
The captured guide's discouraged Tokens/Charges wording does not establish a formal API deprecation date or removal schedule.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/apple-pay/apple-pay-recurring, the November capture changes numbering and spacing rather than the recurring-payment behavior in [[source-stripe-apple-pay-recurring]] (diff lines 3-49; old lines 23-47; new lines 24-48). Both captures explain prompt customer-initiated cryptogram use, later off-session merchant-initiated transactions, and SetupIntent validation. I recommend a corrective source update because the existing summary independently exaggerates several claims, not because Stripe announced a new capability.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/apple-pay/apple-pay-recurring, [[source-stripe-apple-pay-recurring]] should retain the Checkout/Elements automation and SetupIntent free-trial guidance (old lines 8-43; new lines 9-44), but narrow its wording: DPAN can deactivate on device change, a failed CIT makes later MITs likely to fail, and Stripe discourages legacy Tokens/Charges rather than formally deprecating them (old lines 19, 27, 47; new lines 20, 28, 48). The on-session saved-method restriction remains at old line 82 and new line 81.
